newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Euro Central Bank may accept large FX moves - IMF.
newsitem.headline: Euro Central Bank may accept large FX moves - IMF.

text.p: The future European Central Bank (ECB) may let the euro fluctuate more against the dollar and yen than European Union members now allow, International Monetary Fund (IMF) deputy managing director Stanley Fischer suggested.

In a speech prepared for delivery at a financial seminar, Fischer said the issue of whether the euro would be a strong or weak currency depended mainly on the ECB's monetary policy and the mix between fiscal and monetary policy in the euro area.
An IMF representative read the address in the absence of Fischer, who had to stay in Washington because of the crisis over the Thai baht.

"The conventional wisdom is that, because the euro zone is a closed economic area, compared with its individual members or the Federal Republic of Germany itself much less weight will be given to the exchange rate by the ECB in monetary policy decisions," he said.

"Indeed, within its explicit statutory mandate for price stability and within the authority on the exchange rate regime attributed to the Council of Ministers, the Maastricht prescription is heavily biased, even more than in the case of the Bundesbank, toward internal objectives."
With its explicit responsibility to keep prices stable and regime of floating exchange rates, the EBC will be free to decide its stance toward the exchange rate, Fischer said.

"As the latter impact on inflation will be lower than, for instance, in the case of Germany today, it follows that the ECB will be prepared to accept larger exchange rate fluctuations vis-a-vis the two major currencies, the dollar and the yen," he said.

"Volatility among these currencies, and in particular between the euro and the U.S. dollar, is most likely to increase, generating perhaps the need for closer coordination at the international level."
